messages:
Tomo (Support): DeltaHealth reported a regression after we switched embeddings to model-v2. Latency and token costs spiked, and two endpoints returned intermittent 502s for ~30m. Ticket DH-443. Can we triage and decide hotfix vs scheduled release? @Maya

Maya (Product): Do we know root cause yet — model artifact mismatch or routing fallback? Any customer-visible data I can pass to AM?

Tomo (Support): Logs show a sudden spike of fallback to hosted-small variant for some requests. Looks like routing policy matched an old model tag and triggered double-generation in a subset of flows. Snippet from the support trace:```
2026-03-18T16:04:02Z request=dh-req-12 fallback=hosted-small double_call=true
2026-03-18T16:04:03Z cost_tokens=1200 latency_ms=2400 status=502
```

Alistair (Engineering): I can prepare a rollback PR that flips the routing rule to the previous stable tag. It's a config-only change (no model retrain) but the router change touches global routing table; risk is brief incorrect routing for other customers during rollout. PR ETA ~30m, canary ~15m to validate.

Sophie (Sales): DeltaHealth is on premium SLA and is asking for immediate remediation. They want either a hotfix or explicit rollback + comms. They want ETA for resolution to pass to their ops team.

Leo (Eng-Oncall): If customer requests immediate fix, full rollback is fastest. Canary is safer but adds time. What is the blast radius if we do full rollback?

Alistair (Engineering): Full rollback is a single config flip, ~2–3m outage window for routing cache refresh. Canary plan: target 10% traffic for 15m, monitor error rate and cost metrics, then ramp. Canary should surface the regression without impacting all customers.

Maya (Product): Proposed plan: 1) Apply targeted canary rollback to 10% now. 2) Run smoke tests & monitor for 15m. 3) If error rate >0.5% or costs remain elevated, escalate to full rollback. 4) Prepare a follow-up fix in next weekly release to make routing tag validation stricter. Sophie, please notify DeltaHealth with the plan (ETA ~30m). Leo, own oncall monitoring. Alistair, open the PR and tag deploy.

Alistair (Engineering): Opening PR: r-backout/dh-1748722468, will include canary rollout flags. Canary config I will use:```yaml
canary: true
percentage: 10
duration: 15m
criteria:
  error_rate_threshold: 0.5%
  p50_latency_threshold_ms: 1200
```

Sophie (Sales): Sending note to DeltaHealth now: "We are applying a targeted rollback to 10% of traffic for the next 15 minutes to validate. We will update you in 30 minutes or sooner if we need a full rollback." :ear:

Maya (Product): Agreed. Also add a quick regression test to the e2e suite for routing-tag matching; ticket created RT-812 for PM backlog.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary rollback r-backout/dh-1748722468 -> applying to 10% traffic. CI: passed.

Leo (Eng-Oncall): 10m into canary: error rate dropped from 1.2% to 0.12%, token cost per req back to baseline. Monitoring dashboards: https://redwood.internal/dh-443.

Alistair (Engineering): Good signal. Ramp to 50% now.

deploy-bot: Canary ramp to 50% -> success. No new errors in last 5m.

Sophie (Sales): DeltaHealth updated: "We see improvements on our end, thanks. Please confirm when fully rolled back."

Alistair (Engineering): Ramping to 100% now. PR merged and tagged: r-backout/dh-1748722468 -> merged to prod routing config.

Maya (Product): Decision summary: Applied targeted canary rollback, validated with metrics, ramped to 100%, merged PR. Follow-ups: add routing-tag validation to weekly release (RT-812), add a regression test to e2e, and update runbook for canary thresholds. Sophie to send final comms to customer and close DH-443 when done. :white_check_mark:

Tomo (Support): Noted, will close the ticket once Sophie confirms comms sent. Thanks everyone.

Maya (Product): Great work — short postmortem + action items in RT-812. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
